components.cost_effect: 2S uncached component-vector evaluations and S index draws per round; initialization remains separate.
components.goal: Accumulate changes in the target vector rather than re-estimate it from scratch each round.
components.key_estimate: The conditional variance of the centered batch increment is at most L_B^2||x_k-x_{k-1}||^2/S under the linked Theorem's assumptions.
components.name: Same-index sampled increment
components.operation: Average B_i(x_k)-B_i(x_{k-1}) over a fresh with-replacement batch and add to V_{k-1}.
components.requires: Two-point reuse of each sampled component and predictable query points; full-history independent sampling for the linked MSE statement.
transfer_checks: Check same-index two-point access rather than unrelated fresh single-point responses.
Check conditional independence from the entire prior history, not only the point sequence.
Re-establish the increment variance bound under any changed sampling law or Oracle coupling.

limitations.statement: The printed source Eq.(2.6) is not silently corrected. This record uses an explicit full-history fresh-batch formulation whose bound has a separate complete local argument.
Requires same-index two-point evaluations; an Oracle restricted to unrelated fresh single-point samples does not directly implement this rule.
No optimization convergence rate, periodic-refresh complexity, lower bound or unrestricted Oracle Complexity claim is included.

performance_links.scope_note: Finite-uniform predictable-path fresh-batch MSE only; acceptance of the linked local argument is a dependency of accepting this performance claim.

variants.cost: Direct implementation uses S index draws and 2S component-vector evaluations per round, hence KS draws and 2KS evaluations per segment, plus initialization cost C_init. Exact-mean initialization, if chosen, costs n evaluations. Vector arithmetic is O(Sm) per round and can stream with O(d+m) working storage apart from external path-generation/Oracle state. These arithmetic/storage counts are direct implementation accounting, not a separate source complexity theorem; index sampling and Oracle-internal work are separately charged. Caching duplicate queries can change realized calls; 2S is the uncached implementation count.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF p.7 batch notation; p.8 recursion immediately before Lemma 1. Full-history fresh-batch interpretation is explicit local sufficient-condition specialization.
variants.name: Fresh iid with-replacement finite-uniform tracking segment
variants.output: Return V_k after each round as an estimate of B(x_k), with terminal output V_K. The component does not generate the point path and has no optimization-feasibility or stationarity output claim.
public_inputs: n and evaluation access to B_i:R^d->R^m
Positive integer batch size S and segment length K
Initial point x_0 and initial estimate V_0
A sequence of pre-draw predictable points x_1,...,x_K; bounds L_B and epsilon_1 when invoking the MSE guarantee
variants.query_and_update: At k=1,...,K, first receive or select x_k measurably from the pre-draw history. Draw I_{k,1},...,I_{k,S} iid uniformly from [n]. For every j query B_{I_{k,j}}(x_k) and B_{I_{k,j}}(x_{k-1}) with the same index. Compute V_k=V_{k-1}+S^{-1}sum_j[B_{I_{k,j}}(x_k)-B_{I_{k,j}}(x_{k-1})]. Retain x_k,V_k for the next round.
variants.requirements: Fresh iid uniform samples from [n] with replacement, independent of the complete pre-draw history. The Oracle must evaluate the same B_i at x_k and x_{k-1}. The performance link additionally requires the full conditions in thm.P038.tracking_mse, including mean-square Lipschitz increments and ||x_k-x_{k-1}||<=epsilon_1 almost surely.
variants.state_and_initialization: Store x_0 and V_0. The component accepts V_0 as input and requires finite initial MSE for its performance claim. Section 2 does not prescribe its construction. A caller may compute the exact finite mean B(x_0) using n evaluations, yielding zero initial error; this is an optional implementation choice, not a compulsory source initialization rule.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: S and K are caller-supplied positive integers; stop after K updates. This isolated §2 component supplies no target-accuracy stopping rule, periodic refresh schedule or optimization step-size rule. Selecting S,K for a desired MSE requires the explicit Theorem and a bound on initial error.

use_restrictions: Fresh-batch full-history conditions are explicitly supplied sufficient conditions, not a verbatim reading of printed Eq.(2.6).
Performance is conditional on the linked Theorem's complete assumptions and its independent review; no Reviewer acceptance or publication is claimed.
Direct arithmetic/storage accounting and optional exact initialization are distinguished from source assertions.

links.note: MSE for the explicitly specified fresh-batch tracking variant; requires independent acceptance of the complete local argument.

title: SPIDER fresh-batch path-tracking component
